# The conference timezone is the only timezone

## The ruling (Atin, 2026-08-14)

> The conference time zone is the only time zone, and we should display what time zone if
> necessary, if relevant. But generally speaking, this is one event, this one event happens
> in one time zone, we use that time to schedule that event. It's a universal thing.

One event, one clock. Every time an organizer **sets** and every time a human **reads** is
conference-local. Neither the browser's zone nor the Worker's zone may ever decide what a
conference time means. Where the reader could reasonably be elsewhere, name the zone.

## What set this off, and the worse one underneath it

sbek round 11 (`eval:2026-08-14T14-46-26:call-for-papers:2`) filed the CFP close date: an
organizer typed `2027-04-30 23:59`, saved, and the field redisplayed `05/01/2027, 03:59`.
`datetime-local` carries no zone, so both ends must agree on one, and these disagreed —
`src/ui/forms/FormsPage.tsx:493` writes with `new Date(value).getTime()` (**browser-local**)
and reads with `toISOString().slice(0,16)` (**UTC**). The stored instant was right; the
read-back lied.

PR #244 fixed that control by making both ends browser-local. It is **closed**, superseded
by the ruling above — but its branch `mrq-eval11-closedate` is preserved and its test file
`tests/unit/forms-close-date.eval11.test.ts` is a working starting point: it already pins a
non-UTC zone and covers a DST round trip. Read the PR and the branch before starting.

**The same fault has a second instance that is strictly worse.**
`src/ui/submissions/SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:660` places a session on the agenda from a
`datetime-local` parsed as `new Date(schedule.starts_at).getTime()` — browser-local — while
*every* downstream reader of `sessions.starts_at` (agenda grid, portal, ICS, board, public
schedule) renders it in `events.timezone`. An organizer in London placing a talk at "09:00"
for a New York conference schedules it for **04:00**. That is not a read-back fault; the
wrong instant is stored, and the talk is genuinely at the wrong time. `AgendaPage` does this
correctly via `zonedStart`; this screen does not.

## What is already right — do not churn it

A large part of the codebase already does exactly what the ruling asks. Leave it alone and
copy its patterns:

| Already conference-zoned | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Agenda grid, day/time derivation | `src/ui/agenda/track-board.tsx:124` `localParts`, `src/ui/agenda/AgendaPage.tsx:92` `zonedStart` |
| ICS `DTSTART;TZID=` + `X-WR-TIMEZONE` | `src/jobs/calendar/ics.ts:99` `localDateTime`, `src/lib/public-ics.ts:21` |
| Speaker portal slot day/time/leave-by | `src/routes/portal.routes.ts` (3 `Intl` calls, `timeZone: event.timezone`), `src/ui/portal/PortalPage.tsx:247` |
| Board and record slot rendering | `src/api/board.ts:217`, `src/routes/submission-record.routes.ts:171,181` |
| Public schedule clock + starring | `src/ui/public/agenda/schedule-script.ts:84` |
| Conflict detection, venue geometry, file-export folder names | `src/lib/conference-dates.ts:36`, `src/lib/venue-geometry.ts:95`, `src/routes/files-export.routes.ts:87,225` |
| Round-close day key | `src/routes/evaluation.routes.ts:280` `localDayKey` |

`Intl.DateTimeFormat` with an explicit `timeZone` is therefore already **proven on
Cloudflare Workers** — `src/jobs/calendar/ics.ts` runs there and the ICS tests assert its
output. No new dependency is needed and none should be added: `package.json` carries no
date library (hono, preact, zod, aws4fetch only), and `zonedStart`/`localParts` are a
working DST-correct inverse pair already in the tree.

## The zone itself

- `events.timezone TEXT NOT NULL` — `migrations/0001_init.sql:21`. Never null.
- Validated as a real IANA zone on create and update: `assertTimezone`,
  `src/routes/event-settings.routes.ts:247`, called at `:458` and `:553`. A bad zone is a
  422, so an invalid value cannot reach a reader through the API.
- **Reachable from any shell screen with no plumbing**: `useEventContext().event.timezone`
  (`src/ui/shell/event-context.tsx:24,177`). `EventProvider` is mounted at `ShellEntry`
  (`src/ui/app.tsx:53,80`) precisely so it also reaches `/delivery-health`.
- `event` is `null` while the events list is loading. **Do not fall back to the browser's
  zone** — that reintroduces this bug intermittently and invisibly. Render the placeholder
  the surface already uses for absent values (`—`, or the reserved-space span) until the
  zone is known.
- Public surfaces already carry it: `PublicEvent.timezone` (`src/lib/public-site.ts:28`),
  so `PublicEmbedData.event.timezone` is in scope inside `EmbedPage`.
- **Not carried on the public form payload.** `PublicFormState.conference` is
  `{ name, slug }` only (`src/routes/public-form.types.ts:45`). The query that builds it
  already joins the events table (`src/routes/public-form.shared.ts:248`), so this is one
  extra selected column plumbed through `:287` and `:359`.

### A defect found on the way in

`src/ui/settings/EventSettings.tsx:269` offers **four** timezone options (New York, Los
Angeles, London, UTC) while `src/ui/setup/CreateConferencePage.tsx:27` offers **eight**
(adding Chicago, Denver, Berlin, Tokyo, Sydney). A conference created in `Asia/Tokyo` opens
its own settings and the select shows `America/New_York` — the screen states the wrong zone
for the conference. `CreateConferencePage:296` already handles this correctly with
`[...new Set([timezone, ...TIMEZONES])]`. Fix it the same way, from one shared list. In a
build where the conference zone becomes the only zone, the screen that reports it must not
be able to misreport it.

## Consumer inventory

**BEHAVIOUR** = changing it moves a stored instant, or moves when something fires.
**DISPLAY** = the stored instant is unchanged and only the rendering is wrong.

### BEHAVIOUR — a wrong instant gets stored or acted on

| # | Site | Today | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | `src/ui/submissions/SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:660` | `new Date(value).getTime()` — browser-local → `sessions.starts_at` | Conference-zone wall clock → instant. Reuse the same conversion `AgendaPage.zonedStart` uses. |
| B2 | `src/ui/forms/FormsPage.tsx:493` (write half) | `new Date(value).getTime()` — browser-local → `forms.closes_at` | Conference-zone wall clock → instant. **This genuinely moves when the CFP closes and when the reminder fires** for any organizer outside the conference zone — by design, and it is the correction, not a regression. |
| B3 | `speaker_tasks.due_at` enforcement — `src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:88` (`due_at < ?`) against storage from `src/lib/task-due.ts:19` (end of **UTC** day) | A task due "May 1" goes overdue at 23:59:59.999Z = **19:59 EDT on May 1** | A speaker gets their whole day in the conference zone. Either derive the enforcement boundary from the calendar day + `events.timezone` at query time (the query has `task.event_id`; it needs a `JOIN events`), or migrate storage. Prefer the former — it changes no stored row. |

The `forms.closes_at` gates themselves are **already correct and need no change** — every
one is a pure instant comparison, which is zone-free by construction:
`src/routes/public-form.shared.ts:234-239`, `src/lib/public-site.ts:980-981`,
`src/routes/forms.routes.ts:239,510`, `src/routes/portal.routes.ts:1121`,
`src/lib/delivery-health.ts:586`, and the reminder window at
`src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:42-43`. Do not touch them. The only behaviour that moves is what
instant B2 writes.

### DISPLAY — the instant is right, the rendering is wrong

| # | Site | Today | Required |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `src/ui/forms/FormsPage.tsx:493` (read half) | `toISOString().slice(0,16)` — UTC | Conference-zone wall clock, symmetric with B2. **This is the reported bug.** |
| D2 | `src/ui/public/form/PublicForm.tsx:652` | `new Date(closes_at).toLocaleDateString()` — browser-local | Conference zone. Needs the payload change above. |
| D3 | `src/ui/public/form/PublicForm.tsx:69` `closeLabel` | `Intl` with no `timeZone` — browser-local | Conference zone. Same payload. |
| D4 | `src/ui/embeds/EmbedPage.tsx:303` `formatDeadline`, called at `:414` via `cfpBody(:409)` | `Intl` with no `timeZone` | Conference zone. `data.event.timezone` is already in scope in `EmbedPage:427`; thread it through `cfpBody`. **This one is embedded on third-party sites — the reader is definitionally elsewhere, so it must carry a zone label.** |
| D5 | `src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:68` | `"form.closes_at": new Date(...).toISOString()` | The mail body literally reads `2027-05-01T03:59:00.000Z` (template: `src/jobs/mail/templates.ts:50`, "The form closes on {{form.closes_at}}"). Render conference-local, human, zone-labelled. Query needs `events.timezone`. |
| D6 | `src/jobs/mail/schedule.ts:115` | `"task.due_date": ...toISOString()` | Same. |
| D7 | `src/jobs/mail/merge-data.ts:47-51` | `session.time` and `task.due_date` are raw ISO, while `session.leaveBy` at `:29-35` is already zone-aware | Make all three consistent. `RecipientMergeContext` already carries `timezone`. |
| D8 | `src/ui/settings/EventSettings.tsx:269` | Four-option select misreports the conference's own zone | One shared list, plus the current value unioned in. |

### Leave as-is — and say why in the ticket's own words

These render **system and audit** timestamps, not conference times: when a webhook fired,
when a token was last used, when a comment was posted, when a review was saved. The reader
is the person at the keyboard, and their own clock is the right one.

`src/ui/settings/WebhooksPage.tsx`, `src/ui/settings/ApiTokensPage.tsx`,
`src/ui/comms/CommsScreen.tsx:119`, `src/ui/health/DeliveryHealthPage.tsx:67,71`,
`src/ui/files/FileComments.tsx`, `src/ui/portal/FileComments.tsx`,
`src/ui/files/FileVersions.tsx`, `src/ui/files/FilesPage.tsx`,
`src/ui/speakers/SpeakerFilesPanel.tsx`, `src/ui/onboarding/OnboardingPage.tsx:83,88`,
`src/ui/submissions/record-copy.ts`, `src/ui/review/ReviewerPage.tsx:727,761`,
`src/ui/public/form/PublicForm.tsx:641` ("Saved 3:42 PM" — the submitter's own clock is
correct and a conference zone here would be noise), `src/ui/shell/error-reporting.ts`,
`src/lib/observability/log.ts`, `src/routes/telemetry.routes.ts`.

If a later reviewer disagrees about any single one of these, that is a conversation, not a
defect. What must not happen is a sweeping find-and-replace that drags audit timestamps
into the conference zone and makes "when did this webhook fire" unanswerable from the
operator's own desk.

## The UTC contract: it coexists, and here is why

`76eb02e7` (#233) — "CONTRACT · reviewer round close dates use UTC calendar days" — and
`MRQ-114` (`src/lib/task-due.ts`) both pin to UTC deliberately. **The ruling does not
overturn them, because they were never really about UTC.**

Read their own reasons: *"a due date the organizer types must be the due date they read
back"* (`tests/unit/task-due.MRQ-114.test.ts:1-7`) and *"a review round that opens a day
early is a wrong answer, not a rounding one"* (`src/ui/evaluation/EvaluationPage.tsx:29-33`).
Both chose **one agreed anchor instead of the reader's machine** — which is precisely what
the ruling demands. UTC was the mechanism; the intent is identical.

They stay because a **calendar day is not a timezone-bearing value.** "The round closes
May 1" is the same sentence in New York and Tokyo. These fields are `<input type="date">`
with no clock (`EvaluationPage.tsx:717-718`, `TaskTemplatesPage.tsx:311`); the ruling
governs *times*, and there is no time here for a zone to apply to. Two facts settle it:

1. **Nothing gates on evaluation round dates.** `opens_at`/`closes_at` are read and
   returned, never compared to `now` — `src/routes/review.routes.ts:52,56,165,394,627,755`,
   `src/ui/review/ReviewerPage.tsx:670`. They are pure display.
2. **Re-anchoring would silently shift every stored row by a day.** `fromDateInput` stores
   `Date.UTC(y,m,d)` (`EvaluationPage.tsx:45`); rendered in `America/New_York` that midnight
   is 20:00 the *previous* day. Changing the anchor without a migration corrupts every
   existing round date and task due date in place — the exact class of error the original
   contract was written to prevent.

**So: keep the encoding, restate it in the ruling's language.** Calendar-day fields
(`evaluation_rounds.opens_at/closes_at`, `speaker_tasks.due_at`, `events.starts_on/ends_on`)
are **calendar days encoded at UTC midnight**, rendered with no clock and no zone label,
identical for every reader. Update the comments at `EvaluationPage.tsx:29-33` and `:194-198`,
`ReviewerPage.tsx:252-255`, and `task-due.ts:1-12` to say *that*, so the next agent reading
"UTC" does not think it contradicts the ruling and re-open this.

The one place the calendar-day encoding still leaks into behaviour is **B3** — end-of-UTC-day
enforcement of task due dates. Fix the boundary, keep the encoding.

**This is the one item worth an operator sanity-check.** If Atin wants round dates and task
due dates re-anchored to the conference zone outright, that is a separate migration ticket,
not a line in this one.

## DST is not optional

The conference zone's offset changes. **Any implementation using a fixed offset is wrong**,
and it will pass every test written in July.

- Use `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with an explicit `timeZone` for instant → wall clock, and the
  fixed-point iteration in `AgendaPage.zonedStart:93-109` for wall clock → instant. Both are
  already in the tree, both handle DST, and both run on Workers.
- **Never** derive an offset once and reuse it.
- `zonedStart` iterates three times toward a fixed point. Two edge cases are worth an
  explicit decision and a test: a wall-clock time that **does not exist** (02:30 on a
  spring-forward morning) and one that occurs **twice** (fall-back). Pick a documented
  behaviour — settling forward on the gap and taking the first occurrence on the overlap is
  the conventional answer — and assert it rather than leaving it to whatever the loop
  happens to do.
- The design must not depend on the runtime's own zone, in either direction. Browser-local
  and Worker-local are both wrong answers; every call passes `timeZone` explicitly. (The
  Worker's own zone is UTC, which is exactly why this bug was invisible server-side — but
  nothing you write should care.)

## Where the zone gets displayed

The ruling says *"display what time zone if necessary, if relevant."* It is relevant exactly
where the reader might not be in the conference's zone and the value has a clock:

**Label it:**
- The CFP close date in the form builder (`FormsPage`) — the organizer is setting a deadline
  and may be travelling. `Close date (America/New_York)` on the field, or `EDT` beside the
  control.
- The session start on `SubmissionRecordPage` — same reason, higher stakes.
- The public form's "Closes …" (`PublicForm`) — submitters are worldwide.
- The embed CFP deadline (`EmbedPage`) — rendered on someone else's site.
- Times in outbound mail (`schedule.ts`, `merge-data.ts`) — read anywhere, days later,
  with no page around them to give context.

**Do not label it:**
- Inside the agenda builder grid, where every cell is conference-local and a repeated zone
  tag is noise. One statement of the zone in the surface's chrome is enough.
- Calendar-day values (round dates, task due dates) — no clock, no zone.
- System and audit timestamps — those are the reader's own clock by design.

Prefer the short form (`EDT`) inline and the IANA name where the surface has room. Derive it
with `Intl.DateTimeFormat(..., { timeZoneName: "short" })` rather than a hand-written map —
a hand-written map is a fixed offset wearing a disguise.

## Sequencing — display first, behaviour second

Land these as separate commits, and preferably separate PRs. They carry very different risk.

**Step 1 — the shared seam (no behaviour change).**
Extract the working pair into `src/lib/event-time.ts`: `zonedStart` from
`AgendaPage.tsx:92` and `localParts` from `track-board.tsx:124`, plus the `datetime-local`
round-trip pair built on them and a zone-label helper. Both current call sites re-import
from the new home; their behaviour is unchanged and their existing tests must stay green.
One home, so the next surface that needs this does not invent a fourth convention.

**Step 2 — display (safe, shippable alone).**
D1–D8. Nothing stored changes. This alone closes the sbek finding.

**Step 3 — behaviour (real, reviewable, riskier).**
B1, B2, B3. B1 is the most important change in this ticket. Say plainly in the PR that B2
moves when reminders fire for organizers outside the conference zone.

## Test strategy

The suite must prove correctness **from a machine whose local zone is neither UTC nor the
conference's**. That is the whole point: a test that runs in UTC cannot tell the broken
implementation from the fixed one.

- **Pin the machine zone with `process.env.TZ` in try/finally.** The established pattern is
  `tests/unit/abstract-management.MRQ-169.test.ts:243-257` and the `inNewYork` helper in the
  preserved branch's `tests/unit/forms-close-date.eval11.test.ts:14-22`. Verified working on
  this repo's Node (v26): assigning `process.env.TZ` mid-process moves both `Date` and
  `Intl`'s default zone.
- **Pin it to a third zone.** The old test pinned `America/New_York` — the same zone as the
  fixture conference — which now proves less than it should, because browser-local and
  conference-local coincide. Pin the machine to something that is *neither*, e.g.
  `Asia/Tokyo`, with a `America/New_York` conference. Then browser-local, UTC, and
  conference-local are three distinct answers and only one passes.
- **Always restore in `finally`**, and keep these tests in files whose other tests do not
  depend on the ambient zone — `process.env.TZ` is process-global and `maxConcurrency` is 8
  (`vitest.node.config.ts`).
- **DST both ways.** Round-trip wall-clock values either side of both 2027 transitions, as
  the preserved branch does; a fixed offset must fail at least one. Add the nonexistent-time
  and doubled-time cases from the DST section above.
- **Assert both halves of the read-back bug**, as the branch does: the control reads back
  `2027-04-30`, *and* the stored instant really is `2027-05-01` in UTC. That is what makes
  it legible that storage was never wrong.
- **Worker-side rendering** (`schedule.ts`, `merge-data.ts`) is tested in the worker project,
  where `process.env.TZ` does nothing. Prove those by asserting an explicit expected string
  for a fixture zone — that the mail says the conference-local time, not an ISO stamp.
- **Existing tests that must stay green, unmodified**, because they encode the calendar-day
  contract this ticket deliberately preserves: `tests/unit/task-due.MRQ-114.test.ts`,
  `tests/unit/abstract-management.MRQ-169.test.ts:242` ("reviewer round close uses the
  configured calendar day"), `tests/unit/conference-dates.MRQ-142.test.ts`,
  `tests/unit/calendar-ics.AC-95-96-97.test.ts`,
  `tests/integration/attendee-schedule.MRQ-132.test.ts`. **If one of these goes red, the
  change is wrong — do not edit the test.**
- `npm test` and `npm run pr-gate` both green. Read the `status` field, not the wall clock:
  `pass-over-budget` is a warn.

## Non-goals

- **No `Temporal`, no date library.** Zero date dependencies today; keep it that way.
- **No per-user timezone preference.** The ruling is one zone per event, full stop.
- **No storage migration.** No stored instant is rewritten by this ticket. Every stored
  value stays epoch-ms UTC; only interpretation at the edges changes.
- **No re-anchoring of calendar-day fields.** See the contract section. If the operator
  wants it, it is a separate migration ticket.
- **No touching the instant comparisons** that gate form open/close, the portal, delivery
  health, or the reminder window. They are already correct.
- **No sweeping audit/system timestamps into the conference zone.**
- **No API shape change.** `opens_at`/`closes_at`/`starts_at` stay `z.number().int()` epoch
  ms (`src/routes/forms.routes.ts:49-50,132-133`). The API is instant-based and correct.
- **No deploy, no demo reset, no `loop.sh`, no `.deploy-freeze` edit** — an eval round is
  grading a frozen build.

## Acceptance criteria

A builder can check every one of these itself.

1. `src/lib/event-time.ts` exists and is the single home for wall-clock ⇄ instant conversion
   and zone labelling. `AgendaPage` and `track-board` import from it; their existing tests
   pass unmodified.
2. **Grep proves the sweep**: no `datetime-local` control in `src/ui/` writes via
   `new Date(value).getTime()` or reads via `toISOString()`. The two are `FormsPage.tsx:493`
   and `SubmissionRecordPage.tsx:660`.
3. With the machine zone pinned to `Asia/Tokyo` and the conference in `America/New_York`,
   typing `2027-04-30 23:59` into the CFP close date and saving reads back
   `2027-04-30 23:59`, and the value written to `forms.closes_at` is
   `2027-05-01T03:59:00.000Z`.
4. Under the same pinning, placing a session at `09:00` on `SubmissionRecordPage` stores an
   instant that the agenda grid, the portal, and the ICS feed all render as `09:00`.
5. The public form, the embed CFP block, and the outbound reminder mail all state the same
   close moment as the form builder, each in the conference zone. The mail body contains no
   raw ISO 8601 stamp.
6. Every surface listed under "Label it" names the zone; no surface under "Do not label it"
   gained one.
7. `events.timezone` is read from `useEventContext().event.timezone` (or the public payload)
   at every changed site. **No changed site falls back to the browser's or the Worker's zone
   when the event is not yet loaded** — it renders the surface's existing empty placeholder.
8. `src/ui/settings/EventSettings.tsx` and `src/ui/setup/CreateConferencePage.tsx` offer the
   same timezone list from one shared constant, and a conference whose zone is outside that
   list still displays its own zone as the selected value.
9. Calendar-day fields are untouched in storage, and the comments at
   `EvaluationPage.tsx:29-33` / `:194-198`, `ReviewerPage.tsx:252-255`, and `task-due.ts:1-12`
   state the calendar-day rule in the ruling's language rather than justifying "UTC".
10. A speaker task due `2027-05-01` for a `America/New_York` conference is not overdue at
    `2027-05-01T20:00:00-04:00`, and is overdue at `2027-05-02T00:00:01-04:00`.
11. DST: wall-clock round trips hold either side of both 2027 US transitions, and the
    nonexistent-time and doubled-time cases have a documented, asserted behaviour.
12. The five named existing test files pass unmodified. `npm test` and `npm run pr-gate`
    report `pass` or `pass-over-budget`.
13. The 11-step walkthrough loop still completes with zero dead ends.

## Follow-ups — record here, do not mint a second ticket

- Re-anchoring calendar-day fields to the conference zone, with a storage migration, if the
  operator overrules the contract resolution above.
- A conference-zone clock in the shell chrome ("It is 14:20 in New York"), so an organizer
  working from elsewhere always has the conference's time in view.
- Auditing whether any of the "leave as-is" audit timestamps genuinely wants the conference
  zone, one at a time and with a reason each.
- A lint or `check:` script that fails on a `datetime-local` control whose handlers do not
  route through `src/lib/event-time.ts`, so the fourth instance of this bug cannot be
  written.
data.title: The conference timezone is the only timezone: every organizer-set time is conference-local

data.description:
One ticket of small fixes to the attendee-schedule prototype and its design contract, from the v0.2 adversarial review (prototypes/attendee-schedule/REVIEW-v0.2.md, in the working tree — deliberately uncommitted) as ruled by Atin, 2026-08-14, in conversation with the review agent. This ticket is self-contained: everything needed is below; the review file is background only.

SCOPE
- prototypes/attendee-schedule/index.html: v0.2 → v0.3 (bump the badge + header comment)
- sequence/attendee-schedule-design.md: two §7 ruling amendments (text provided below)
- No src/ changes. This is prototype + design-doc work; the build inherits it later.

FIXES + ACCEPTANCE

1. Move the public star count out of the star rail.
   The count currently renders under the star button, where it reads as a like counter that never moves when you tap. Move it to the right-hand meta column as a quiet "★ 412" beside the format/track chips (same register as the detail page's "★ 176 attendees"). The star cell goes back to button-only. Threshold/off states still reserve space — elements never jump. Detail page unchanged.

2. Unlink honesty (ruling + copy).
   Ruled semantics (add to §7, wording below): unlink deletes what the claim created and only that — the email↔schedule-code linkage always; the claim-sourced event_attendances row; the person row only if this claim minted it and nothing else is attached. Import-sourced rows are untouched.
   Prototype: after Unlink, show one plain confirmation line in the claim row (same honesty register as the claim disclosure): "Unlinked — your email and picks are removed from the organizers' records." before returning to the empty-input state (or as a transient state of it). No jump: the row keeps its reserved height.

3. Organizer door marked as a demo surface.
   Footer link text → "Organizer view (demo) ↗". The demand view opens with one line under the heading: "Admin surface — shown in the prototype for the walkthrough; behind organizer sign-in in the product."

4. Demand bar re-gauged to capacity.
   The bar currently scales to the max-starred session while the chip shows % of capacity — two scales in one row, and the one over-subscribed session gets one of the shortest bars. Make the bar = % of room capacity with a hairline tick at 100%; fill past the tick renders in the warn/alarm tone. Sort order and the count column keep carrying popularity. (Keep tones as CSS in the prototype; note for build: status-trio tokens, no literals.)

5. Agent-built schedules feed the demand signal (ruling + copy).
   Ruled mechanism (add to §7, wording below): demand count = distinct beacon devices + distinct API-created schedule codes containing the session. Web clients send their device hash with POST/PUT /schedules so synced codes de-dup against their own device; an agent's POST carries no device hash and counts as one.
   Prototype: For-agents sheet gains the line "Building a schedule counts toward the session demand signal (anonymously)." Organizer stats row gains a "via agents" figure so the board shows the signal exists.

6. Mock numbers reconcile.
   The org stats say 2,570 stars placed; the demand board sums to 1,950. Make the gauges agree (adjust the stat, or rebalance STARS — keep the two seeded sub-threshold sessions and the one over-capacity room). Keep the mini-table arithmetic consistent (3 shown + 2,057 more = 1,847 imported + 213 claimed). If a "via agents" stat is added (#5), fold it into the same arithmetic.

7. Polish batch (all ruled in):
   - Resend → "Sent" swap must not shift the Unlink button: give the quiet buttons a fixed/min width (elements never jump).
   - Import prompt step 3: active voice, state the contract — the import endpoint writes the attendance rows itself when the event is passed; the agent does not make a second call.
   - Demand-board session titles get a hover affordance (underline on hover/focus, like agenda titles).
   - Aria/tooltip: org toggle role="switch" uses aria-checked (not aria-pressed); star button aria-label keeps the session title after toggling; the public count gets screen-reader-accessible text; count tooltip copy becomes "N schedules include this session" (honest vs the distinct-devices/codes truth — replaces "N attendees have starred").

§7 AMENDMENT TEXT (append under a "Round-2 review rulings (Atin, 2026-08-14)" subheading; adjust prose to fit the doc voice):
- Unclaim: Unlinking deletes what the claim created and only that — the email/schedule-code linkage always, the claim-sourced attendance row, and the person row only if the claim minted it and nothing else references it. Import-sourced people and attendance rows are never touched by unlink. The unlink confirmation states this plainly, in the same register as the claim disclosure.
- Agent demand: the demand aggregate counts distinct beacon devices plus distinct API-created schedule codes containing the session. Web clients pass their device hash when creating/updating a schedule so a synced code de-dups against its device; agent-created codes (no device hash) count as one. The For-agents doc discloses that building a schedule contributes anonymously to the demand signal.
- Public count semantics: the viewer's own star is part of the aggregate (their device is a distinct device) but the number is a server aggregate refreshed on render, not a live tally; the count renders as session metadata (beside the chips), not under the star button, precisely so it does not read as a like counter.

EXPLICITLY OUT OF SCOPE (operator rulings, same session):
- Threshold n=0 showing "0"s: fine as is.
- Prototype dates stay Oct 13–15; demo data, no shift to Oct 12–14.
- CRM mock emails in the organizer view: demo data, fine as is.

VALIDATION (in_validation gate)
Drive http://127.0.0.1:8123/attendee-schedule/index.html (c11 embedded browser or equivalent): star a counted session and confirm the count sits with the chips and the star cell doesn't move; run claim → unlink and read the confirmation line; check the demand board's over-capacity row now has the longest-past-tick bar; flip the public-counts toggle both ways; confirm Resend/Sent doesn't shift Unlink. Then clear the three localStorage keys (marquee:proto:attendee-schedule, :org, :claim) so the operator's next drive is a cold start with the demo defaults (counts ON via the seeded default).

data.description:
THE build ticket for the attendee-schedule rounds 2+3 design, signed off by Atin 2026-08-14. One solid ticket, one Opus delegator, whole loop (operator ruling — round-1 precedent MRQ-132).

CONTRACT (read in this order; all committed on main)
1. sequence/attendee-schedule-design.md — §7 in full: R2-1…R2-5, the design section, Constraints, the round-2 review rulings, Round 3, and the Round-4 build rulings (design signed off; claim = request → verify; retention = persist indefinitely; demand board = Agenda-module panel; speaker pins derived never stored; mail launch-gated).
2. prototypes/attendee-schedule/index.html at v0.3 — the BINDING visual contract; the build reproduces its round-2/3 surfaces one-to-one in the Flight Deck skin (DESIGN.md; tokens in src/styles/tokens.css — every color a token, no literals; check:design must pass).
3. DESIGN.md + PHILOSOPHY.md — craft rules bind (elements never jump; tabular numerals; honest empty/loading states; speed is a feature R7).
4. Round-1 shipped code (MRQ-132, PR #102) — the star module, schedules short-code API, My Schedule view, ICS/webcal are LIVE; this ticket extends them, never forks them.

DELIVERABLES
1. D1 migration: event_attendances join (person_id, event_id, source import|claim, schedule_code nullable, verified_at, timestamps — no memberships/roles change, per §7); star-beacon table (event_id, session_id, device_hash) with idempotent upsert/delete; org-level public-counts setting (on/off default OFF + threshold n, configurable, floor 1, default 3); public_schedules gains nullable device_hash for agent-demand de-dup.
2. Star beacon: anonymous endpoints with their own KV limiter (schedules 30/hr/IP pattern — the shared buckets are a no-op). Demand aggregate per session = distinct device_hash + distinct schedule codes with NULL device_hash containing the session; web clients pass their device hash on POST/PUT /schedules so synced codes de-dup.
3. Public agenda counts: quiet ★-chip beside the format/track chips (NEVER under the star button) at count ≥ n when the setting is on; detail-page inline count; copy "N schedules include this session" with sr text; slot reserved at threshold/off. Setting ships OFF.
4. Claim flow (request → verify, round-4 ruling): "Get it by email" row per prototype; Send = Turnstile + own limiter + one transactional mail carrying the sync URL; NO CRM write at send. First open of the emailed link = verification: person upsert by email, attendance row (source claim, schedule_code, verified_at), identity-line flip. Pending state after send: "Check your email — link sent to …" (acknowledged divergence from the prototype's post-verify state). Resend. Unlink per the unclaim ruling: deletes the email↔code linkage always, the claim-sourced attendance row, and the person row only if the claim minted it and nothing else references it; confirmation copy exactly: "Unlinked — your email and picks are removed from the organizers' records."
5. Identity legibility (round 3): agenda intro "No sign-in…" line; My Schedule identity line in both states (anonymous / linked with masked email + Manage), per prototype.
6. Speaker cross-over (round 3 + round-4 semantics): on VERIFIED claim whose email matches a speaker at the event (same people table — the CRM rail), their speaking sessions pin into My Schedule with "You're speaking" chips — list, glance panel (ink-filled blocks), agent briefing, ICS/webcal set, overlap detection (starring against your own talk warns). Pins are DERIVED at render, never stored in sessionIds; absent from the shared read-only link; unlink removes them.
7. Organizer demand panel, homed in the Agenda module of the admin shell: exact counts including sub-threshold, ranked; bar = % of room capacity with a hairline tick at 100%, past-tick fill in status tokens; "bigger room?" over-capacity chip; stats row (imported / synced / via agents / claimed / advance picks — gauges must reconcile); public-counts setting + threshold control beside it. Room capacity: source from the venue/room model — if rooms carry no capacity field yet, add one (nullable; rows without capacity show the count and an em-dash, no fake ratio).
8. Attendee import + agent affordance: extend the people import rails (org-imports.routes.ts + documented API) to write attendance rows (source import) idempotently by email when an event is passed — the endpoint writes them itself, no second call; re-running never dupes a person. People-surface "task for your agent" block with the pre-filled prompt (prototype's IMPORT_PROMPT as the model, corrected to the real endpoints/paths). Skill-file chapter: export → map → bulk upsert → verify counts.
9. For-agents doc: add the demand-signal disclosure ("Building a schedule counts toward the session demand signal, anonymously") and keep the endpoint enumeration current.

CONSTRAINTS (binding)
- Resend free tier 100/day: claim mail is LAUNCH-GATED — build the send behind a flag, everything else live. Build ≠ enable.
- Privacy posture: anonymous stars stay anonymous forever; identity only at verified claim; NO silent linkage of star data to imported ticket-holders; aggregates carry no identity.
- CRM doctrine: attendees are people rows + event_attendances — no parallel table, no workflow status on people, notes/tags/lists attach to person_id.
- Retention: no TTL machinery — codes and feeds persist.
- Every new anonymous endpoint: own limiter; Turnstile wherever an email is accepted.
- Suite budget 45s / gate budget 120s; read the status field per repo CLAUDE.md.

VALIDATION (in_validation gate — "I saw it work")
Against the running system (browser automation + curl): star → chip appears at threshold when setting on and never under the star; agent loop via curl (POST schedule without device hash raises the demand aggregate by one; with device hash de-dups); claim send → pending state → open the verification link (dev: capture the mail/log) → identity flips, CRM rows exist; unlink → rows removed per ruling, copy exact; speaker cross-over with a seeded speaker email → pins render everywhere ruled, absent from the shared link; demand panel gauges reconcile and the over-capacity row reads loudest. Attach evidence before pr_open.

PROCESS
Linked worktree cut from github/main (never local main; primary checkout is the board home — no branch work there). PR to Stage-11-Agentics/marquee main via gh. A non-author review before merge; merge on green + review (repo rule). Merging does not deploy — DEPLOY.md governs shipping, out of this ticket's scope unless the operator asks.
data.title: Build attendee schedule rounds 2+3 — demand signal, email claim, attendees in CRM, speaker cross-over

data.description: Build the Organization Home page the MRQ-203 nav row points at (Organization group: Home · People CRM · Outreach · Settings). Design contract: prototypes/pipeline-v1.1 v1.15 #org/home + sequence/org-settings-design.md iteration 3 (green-lit by Atin 2026-08-14). A composition, not a system: (1) conferences as seasons — every event with dates/state/headline stats, live one opens /dashboard, plus create; (2) the attention strip — outreach follow-ups overdue (from the next-touch data MRQ-205 builds), seats scoped to ended conferences (governance ticket), server connection state (existing instance status) — each line links to its surface, and each source that does not exist yet renders an honest empty, never a fake number; (3) relationship KPIs — people count, returning speakers (2+ conferences via participations), in-outreach count, organizer count; (4) recent org activity (audit_log, newest 4) linking to the full Activity lens. Server-side queries, R7 budgets apply. MRQ-207 is building the org-settings shell in parallel: mount Home at its own route (per prototype: org home is a page, not a settings tab) so there is no shell dependency.
data.title: Organization Home: the between-conferences view

data.description: Rename the Instance panel to Server in plain organizer language (ruling 2026-08-14, sequence/org-settings-design.md iteration 3; design contract prototypes/pipeline-v1.1 v1.15 #org/server). Head: 'What this Marquee is connected to, and whether each piece is working.' Rows lead with the job — Email sending · File uploads · Spam protection · Web address — service names (Resend, R2, Turnstile) as small print; chips read working / not set up. The mail row names the connected Resend sender and account (derived from real config, never a stored flag — extend GET /api/v1/instance/status if needed) and offers an Open Resend link out. Applies everywhere the panel renders (setup dashboard D8 panel + steady state). Steady-state placement is a tab of the org-settings surface MRQ-207 is building in parallel: if 207 has merged when you integrate, mount there (route org/server, redirect org/instance); otherwise mount behind your own route and say so in the PR. Recovery card copy per prototype ('no passwords, ever').
data.title: Server panel: plain-language connections, named Resend account

data.description: Ruling 2026-08-14 (sequence/org-settings-design.md iteration 3): one audit substrate projected three ways, never three logs. The substrate exists — audit_log (migration 0006, src/lib/audit.ts). (1) Instrument the org-level writers that do not yet record: invite mint/claim/revoke, member removal (with what was revoked), token create/revoke, org default changes, ownership transfer — some of these writers are being built by MRQ-207 and the governance ticket in parallel; instrument what exists on main and leave a named seam the parallel tickets call. (2) Org admin lens: reverse-chron log of admin actions (design: prototype v1.15 #org/activity) — steady-state home is an org-settings tab (MRQ-207 shell; standalone route if 207 unmerged, noted in PR). (3) Person lens: the person record activity feed merges audit rows touching that person with the existing annotations/history. (4) Submission lens: a timeline on the submission record — submitted, routed, reviewed, decided, reversed, re-accepted, mail sent — each with author and timestamp; extend the existing ContentHistory/history machinery rather than inventing parallel storage. Server-side pagination; R7 budgets; tests per lens.
data.title: Activity: one append-only log, three lenses (org admin, person, submission)

data.description: Rulings 2026-08-14 (sequence/org-settings-design.md iteration 3; design contract prototypes/pipeline-v1.1 v1.15 #org/organizers). (1) Role legend as ruled — Owner / Organizer / Ops / Reviewer, one capability line each — rendered on the Organizers surface and live under the invite modal's role picker (the Reviewer line says sign-in only, assign work in Evaluation). UI 'Organizer' maps to schema program_lead; write the mapping down once where roles render. (2) Permission model: the org-settings surface is visible to Owner + org-wide Organizers only; only the Owner removes members; Organizer and up invite. Enforce server-side, reflect in UI (permission-aware action column exactly as the prototype demonstrates). (3) Owner transfer, safe and simple: Owner-only action on their own row; eligible recipients are org-wide Organizers who have signed in; confirm requires the organization name typed back; the flip is immediate and atomic, old owner becomes Organizer, both notified by mail (outbox rules), recorded to audit_log. (4) Stale seats: a seat scoped to an ended conference never expires silently — banner on the Organizers surface + data for the Org Home attention line. Builds directly on MRQ-207's removal-cascade and scoped-invite work — coordinate, do not duplicate.
data.title: Organizer governance: role legend, Owner-only removal, owner transfer, stale seats

data.description: Completes the one-invite-machinery ruling (2026-08-14; design contract prototypes/pipeline-v1.1 v1.15 invite modal + evaluation committee card). (1) The invite modal renders the one-time join link as a real, scannable QR (vendor a minimal zero-dependency QR encoder or generate inline SVG server-side — flag before adding any npm dependency) beside the copyable URL and MRQ-207's short join code. (2) The committee door: Evaluation's Program committee card gains + Invite reviewer, which opens the same invite flow preset to role Reviewer scoped to the current conference — same link, same expiry, same pending row. One machinery, two entry points; no duplicated mint path. Depends on MRQ-207's role+scope invite mint landing first.
data.title: Invite machinery completions: QR code and the committee door

data.description:
Build the sponsor-contact portal designed and loved 2026-08-14. Binding design contract: prototypes/sponsor-portal/index.html (commit 6ab0b7ee) reproduced one-to-one, plus sequence/sponsors-design.md §3.3 and §5 (the round's rulings). Flight Deck rules bind as everywhere; judge's vocabulary is law (Session, Portal, Task).

WHAT IT IS — the speaker portal's sibling: magic-link entry (existing auth), public-shell chrome, SPEC §3.7 task machinery. Center of gravity is the SPONSORSHIP. Page order: head (welcome + N-of-M deliverables meter) → sponsorship hero (company · tier chip · status · derived deal line read from attached data — Sessions count, booth number, passes — never a tier blurb; organizer contact on the right) → booth location card (speaker location-card machinery reused: loc-lines, load-in leave-by box, venue map; rendered only when booth data exists, absence ordinary) → deliverables (task rows with assignee labeling, overdue markers, cancelled-block with reason once) → Sessions cards (read-only) → company profile (org-level, contact roster, Primary/You chips) → sponsor handbook.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (stable AC IDs minted at consolidation):
1. A sponsorship_contact enters by magic link and sees the whole sponsorship: every deliverable with its assignee named ("yours" / "assigned to X").
2. ANY signed-in contact can complete ANY open deliverable; completion records and displays attribution ("completed by <name>"), including when completer ≠ assignee. Chase board reflects immediately.
3. Task kinds render their real payloads (acknowledge / file request / form) with kind-specific validation; cancelled tasks sit below a dashed divider, reason stated once, excluded from progress; completed work is never restyled by cancellation (SPEC §3.7 semantics).
4. Sessions are read-only cards; the task machinery is the single write path ("Name your speaker" completion fills the Session's speaker; "Session title/description" tasks fill content). Honest empties: "Speaker not named yet" links to its task; unscheduled states when scheduling happens; unpublished slots carry "Not yet public".
5. A booth-bearing sponsorship renders the booth card (number, hall, building, load-in window, access note, leave-by line, map); a boothless one simply composes down — no special casing either way (ruling 5).
6. Derived deal line in hero: chips computed from linked Sessions, booth data, passes. Nothing hardcoded per tier — the portal shows the deliverables it is given (tier-scoped content variation is a Later band).
7. Company profile edits write org-level company facts; contacts are read-only in the portal (managed by the organizer), Primary and You marked.
8. Seed/demo data carries BOTH prototype views (operator ruling 2026-08-14: keep the prototype views in the build): a Gold booth-bearing sponsorship with 3 contacts, an overdue task, a cancelled task, one scheduled + one speakerless Session; and a Silver boothless single-contact sponsorship. Both demonstrable end-to-end.
9. Craft: elements never jump (fixed-width task action buttons, reserved states), tabular numerals, honest empty/loading/error states, R7 speed.

DEPENDENCY: requires the sponsors-module data layer (sequence/sponsors-design.md §3.1: companies, sponsor_tiers, sponsorships, sponsorship_contacts, task-join for grouping, nullable sponsorship_id on submissions) and organizer-side surfaces — NOT YET TICKETED. This ticket should be linked blocked_by that ticket when it is minted. Contract-time work: tone-architect to spec the attribution field (completed-by actor on task completion) as a SPEC amendment.

OPERATOR HOLD (Atin, 2026-08-14): do not start a worker on this ticket yet — machine overloaded. Design and cut only.
data.title: Sponsor portal: sponsor-contact portal on the speaker-portal machinery

data.description:
ONE ticket, ONE PR, by operator ruling (2026-08-14): the ≤760px navigation redesign plus every phone-width defect from the mobile QA sweep merge together.

## Binding design
prototypes/mobile-nav/index.html (committed 850ccc58) — drive it. Rulings encoded there:
- ≤760px: the bottom strip is DELETED; nav becomes an overlay drawer off an ink-filled hamburger (primary-action register, 36×30, white 2px lines) top-left in the topbar. 761–1000px icon rail unchanged.
- The drawer is the Sidebar component VERBATIM — CSS repositions it, no second nav implementation. Full parity: brand, conference switcher, group labels, all sidebar rows at 40px touch height, footer.
- Mobile topbar = hamburger + flexing search + avatar, nothing else. Theme select moves into the drawer footer at phone width.
- Dismissal: scrim tap, ✕, Escape, any navigation. aria-modal dialog semantics; focus → ✕ on open, → hamburger on close; page scroll locks; 160ms ease-out, none under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Drawer scrollbar THEMED via tokens (scrollbar-width: thin; scrollbar-color: var(--line-strong) transparent + ::-webkit-scrollbar pair) so dark registers inherit. Never OS-default chrome inside themed chrome.

## Defect register (mobile QA, 390px viewport — full detail in ticket comment M-01..M-22)
Root-cause fixes, in commit order for reviewability:
1. M-01 BLOCKER, fix first: .global-search { width:100% } at ≤760 makes header.topbar 549px wide in a 373px viewport → 176px page-level h-scroll on EVERY admin screen, theme+account off-viewport. Fix: flex:1; min-width:0; theme select to drawer foot. (/reviewer has no topbar and scrolls 373/373 — proof.)
2. Drawer fold itself (see design above). The ≤1000px hides of .event-context-row/.nav-label/.sidebar-foot must band to (max-width:1000px) and (min-width:761px), WRITTEN PREFIX-FIRST so MRQ-203 contract tests' indexOf("@media (max-width: 1000px)") still matches. DeliveryHealthShell mounts Sidebar+Topbar too — wire it identically. .page bottom padding returns to normal (no strip to clear).
3. M-04/M-13/M-14 grid blowout family (BLOCKERS on /dashboard + /delivery-health, major /evaluation): outer grid tracks with auto min-content minimums compute literal 734px/635px columns in 341px containers. minmax(0,1fr) on outer tracks + single-column phone breakpoints on inner grids (344px 344px, 366px 366px, 86px 594px).
4. Touch targets app-wide (M-02/03/09/14/15/16/19 + M-11/M-17 controls): 12px checkboxes, 17-20px inputs/selects, 22-26px chips/tabs/buttons, 15px name-buttons. One breakpoint-scoped pass on shared control geometry: ≥24×24 visual, ≥40px hit at ≤760 (WCAG 2.2 AA floor is 24; Apple floor 44).
5. Tables at phone width (M-07 roster, M-10 onboarding matrix, M-11 comms, M-15 files, M-16 people): the field the screen exists for (STATUS etc.) must be visible without sideways scroll — column-priority or card-collapse. /tasks and /reviewer are the clean references.
6. M-08 + M-15/M-16 pagination: roster/onboarding render all ~508 rows (34,900px docs); /submissions' 50-at-a-time pattern already exists — apply it. R7.
7. Polish where cheap: M-05/M-18 scroll affordances, M-10 chip overflow, M-11 message-status 9px overflow, M-17 name-button above move-select spacing, M-21 public /agenda target sizes. M-06 board stays a kanban scroller (its nested-axis pain dies with M-01); single-column board mode explicitly OUT of scope.

## Acceptance
- At 390px: document.scrollWidth == viewport width on EVERY admin route (the M-20 /reviewer standard).
- Drawer full parity + all dismissal paths + focus discipline as prototyped; strip gone.
- /dashboard and /delivery-health fully readable at rest — "Plan next wave", ACT NOW banner + "Open the list" on-screen.
- Roster STATUS / files STATUS visible without horizontal scroll; roster+onboarding paginate.
- Interactive controls meet the target floor at ≤760.
- MRQ-203 contract tests updated only where the ≤760 contract changed; suite within budget; pr-gate green.
- in_validation: drive the real site at 390px (browser pane) across all admin routes + drawer flows; attach evidence.
data.title: Mobile update: drawer nav + phone-width sweep (single PR)
